turns.t: Hello there, doctor. Lovely to meet you. I'm only here because my daughter nagged me, she says I get puffed out.
Well, I'm glad she nagged. What does she mean by puffed out? ~
It's only when I carry my shopping, you see. Up the hill from the Co-op, two bags, and by the top I've got to stop and catch my breath.
How long has that been happening, would you say?
Oh, a few months, maybe since the spring. I thought I was just getting old. I'm sixty-eight, you know.
That's not old. Does it ever happen when you're walking without the bags?
Not really, no. Only when I'm laden. I did the Pennine Way in my forties, you know, so I like to think I've got a bit of stamina. ~
I'm sure you have. Any chest pain, or tightness, when you're puffed out?
No pain, no. Just short of breath.
And any swelling in your ankles, or waking up at night breathless?
No, I sleep like a log. My ankles are the same as ever.
Good. What tablets are you taking at the moment?
Bisoprolol, 2.5 mg once a day, and ramipril, 5 mg once a day. They're for my blood pressure, I think. Or my heart? One of the two.
Both are good for the heart and the blood pressure, so you're right either way. ~
Ha! Good, I wasn't sure. ~
Do you smoke?
I gave up in 1998, thank goodness. Twenty a day I was smoking, if you can believe it.
Well done. Let me check your pulse and oxygen first. ~
Do you want my wrist or my finger? ~
Just the finger, thanks. Pulse 66 and oxygen 98 percent.
Is that good for a man of my age? ~
It's excellent. Now I'll listen to your heart and lungs. Breathe normally. ~
Does it matter if I talk? ~
Yes, so don't. Take a deep breath in.
Sorry. ~
Your lungs are clear, and your heart sounds are normal, no murmur that I can hear.
Marvellous. So what do you think it is? ~
Breathlessness when you're carrying a heavy load can come from several things, and from what we have so far, I can't rule out early heart failure yet, though it is only a possibility at this stage.
Is that serious? ~
It might not be anything much, and I don't want to put a label on it before the tests. I'd like to arrange an echocardiogram, an ultrasound of your heart.
Like they do for pregnant women? ~
Exactly the same machine, yes. And I'd like to take a blood test to check a heart strain marker and your kidney function, since you're on ramipril.
Do I need to fast? ~
No fasting needed. The surgery will text you when the scan is booked. ~
Right. Should I stop carrying the shopping in the meantime? ~
Not stop, but take it in smaller loads, and rest at the postbox if you need to.
Postbox it is. Do I come back after the tests? ~
Someone from the practice will ring you with the results and we'll agree what to do next. ~
Splendid. Thank you, doctor, you've been very kind. ~

chief_complaint.value: she says I get puffed out

physical_examination.normalized_finding: Clear lungs and normal heart sounds

clinical_actions.description: Carry smaller loads and rest if breathless
